# dsh-cursor
Cursor models inside DeepSeek Harness.
English | 简体中文

`dsh-cursor` registers a DeepSeek Harness LLM provider route named `cursor`.
The models it offers ar

e the ones your Cursor account can select, and the
streams it returns are produced by the Cursor age

nt SDK. Once installed, Cursor
models appear next to every other provider in the Harness model selec

DK. Once installed, Cursor
models appear next to every other provider in the Harness model selector.

> Unofficial integration. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by
> Cursor / Anysphere. U

se it only with accounts you are authorized to use, and
> in line with Cursor's terms of service.
## How it works

Cursor does not publish a chat-completions endpoint. It publishes an **agent**
— a local runtime tha

t owns a prompt, a tool surface, and a model selection.
The Harness instead asks a provider for one

streamed assistant message per
request, with the whole conversation passed in.
This plugin bridges those two shapes:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

* Every request renders the Harness conversation (system prompt, turns, tool
calls and their results

) into **one prompt** for a short-lived Cursor agent.
A request stays a pure function of the session

log, exactly as the Harness
expects.
* **Cursor never touches your machine.** The agent is created

with
`tools: ['mcp']`, so Cursor's own file, shell, search, and subagent tools are
not registered. T

he only tools the model can see are the Harness tools for
this request, bridged as in-process custom

tools.
* When the model asks for one of those tools, the plugin **cancels the Cursor
run** and repo

rts the tool call to the Harness, which executes it with its own
permissions, sandbox, and UI. The r

esult comes back on the next request.
* Text and thinking stream token by token through `onDelta`; t

oken usage is
reported on every turn.
## Install
From GitHub:

or from a local clone / tarball:

The package declares a DSH bundle patch, so installation mounts the provider
automatically. Reload t

he page (or restart `dsh web`) and open **Settings >
Models**: a **Cursor** row appears with its API

r restart `dsh web`) and open **Settings >
Models**: a **Cursor** row appears with its API-key card.

The bundle is not published to npm; install it from GitHub or from a local
checkout. `npx dsh-cursor

login` therefore only works from this repo
(`node bin/cursor-login.mjs login`) or after a global gi

t install — pasting a
key into the card needs no CLI at all.
## API keys

Open **Settings > Models > Cursor**. The Cursor card manages any number of API
keys and chooses whic
h one every request uses:

* **Add key** — paste a key and give it a label. The first key becomes active
automatically.
* The r

adio button selects the **active** key. Requests authenticate as that
key's account, and the model c

atalog follows the active key, so switching
accounts is one click (reopen the model picker to reload

the new account's
models).
* **Replace key** rewrites the stored secret; **Delete** removes the ent

ry and
its stored credential. A label can be edited without touching the secret.
* Key values are se

nt to the Harness credentials service under generated
`CURSOR_KEY_*` references and are never return

ed to the page again. The card
shows the reference and the last four characters only.
* The key list

and the selection live in this plugin's settings, so they survive
restarts; the secrets live in `$D
SH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`.
With no managed key the historic chain still applies, in this order:

1. the key saved in the Models page field (credential `CURSOR_API_KEY`),
2. the `CURSOR_API_KEY` env

ironment variable,
3. the credential a previous `npx dsh-cursor login` stored at
`~/.cursor/sdk/auth

t variable,
3. the credential a previous `npx dsh-cursor login` stored at
`~/.cursor/sdk/auth.json`.

Create keys at <https://cursor.com/dashboard/api>. Team admin API keys are not
supported by the Curs
or SDK; use a user key or a service-account key.

That stored login is the last fallback; a managed key takes precedence once one
exists.
## Models

The catalog comes from `Cursor.models.list()` for the active account — the
selected managed key, or

the fallback credential when no key is managed — and is
cached for ten minutes per credential. Curso

r's per-model parameters are mapped
onto the Harness reasoning selector when the parameter is thinki

ng-shaped
(`thinking`, `reasoning`, `effort`, …).

If discovery cannot run — for example on an air-gapped pilot — list the model
ids explicitly in the
plugin configuration:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## What you get, and what you give up
Working:

* model selection, streaming text, streamed reasoning, token usage
* the full Harness tool surface (

bash, file edits, grep, todos, subagents, MCP
tools, …) with Harness permissions, sandboxing, and ap

proval prompts
* session titles, compaction, and any other auxiliary model call
Deliberate limitations:

* **The transcript is replayed on every request.** Cursor's agent is stateful
and the Harness reques

t is not, so each turn is sent as a full conversation
snapshot. Prompt caching keeps this cheap in p

ractice, but reported input
tokens are higher than a native provider's.
* **Tool calls end the Curso

r run.** The Harness, not Cursor, is the agent that
acts; Cursor's planning between tool calls happe

ns one step at a time.
* **No image input.** Attachments are replaced with a text placeholder, becau

se
the bridged prompt path is text-only.
* **Auxiliary calls are also agent runs.** Session-title ge

neration and
compaction cost one Cursor run each.
* Cursor writes its local agent store under `~/.cu

rsor` as the SDK normally
does; the plugin sets nothing there.
## Compatibility

Targets **DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2`** (`engines.dsh`), Node.js **22.13+**
(required by `@cursor/
sdk`), and `@cursor/sdk` **1.2.x**.
